dossier.architecture: Pass-through two-joint arm, direct station gripper and later full-width cube floor intake.

subsystems.intake: Wide cube collector with compliant centering guides. Floor cone acquisition deliberately omitted in favor of reliable double-substation cycles.
subsystems.transfer: Floor cube intake hands to the arm; duct-taped compliant strap guides replaced stiffer materials that trapped or damaged cubes.
subsystems.scoring: Both arm-joint transmissions mounted low; gripper roller drive counterbalances the distal joint.
subsystems.endgame: Charge-station method is not covered by the retrieved walkthrough.
subsystems.controls: Two AprilTag cameras and a 27-node selector automate community placement; pre-match dashboard checks module configuration and running software threads.

versions: Cube floor intake added after early competition/testing.
Guide materials iterated from rigid shaft and other compliant candidates to the final strap arrangement.
dossier.analysis: A useful explicit omission: floor cones were rejected because alignment cost and defense exposure outweighed their expected benefit for this team's cycles. This is strategic simplification with a stated operational basis.
limits: Endgame details and full configuration chronology remain incomplete.

context_documents.title: 2023-6036 · Deliberately omitted floor cones preserve a reliable preferred cycle
context_documents.body:
# 2023-6036: Deliberately omitted floor cones preserve a reliable preferred cycle

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

A double-jointed arm keeps both joint transmissions low. A wide cube collector uses compliant guides; cones are acquired at the double station rather than through a floor-cone mechanism. Collector material iterations address trapped or damaged cubes.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team chooses arm freedom to permit software iteration and targets rapid pickup-to-setpoint motion. The retained account explicitly omits floor cones in favor of reliable station work.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Missing a task can be a deliberate architectural trade. That trade depends on station access under defense and the cost of a failed floor recovery, not a blanket claim that floor cones lack value.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure defended station cycles, cube handoff damage and arm settle time; provide a recovery plan when station access is blocked.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
